We need answer only valid JSON with keys. Need produce concise architecture plan. Need interpret specs. Need return JSON only, no markdown. Keys: state_machine, timer_plan, priorities, initial_values, scan_execution_order, formal_assertions optional list. Need at most 2000 words. Need complete JSON. Must be valid. Need design for PLC. Let's reason.

We need architecture for Aeration Blower Delayed Start. Inputs DO_LOW, AERATION_E_STOP_NC; outputs BLOWER_RUN bool, AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT UINT. Requirements: start delay when both DO_LOW and E_STOP_NC true (permit). BLOWER_RUN only after conditions remain satisfied for 5s. If DO_LOW false or emergency stop occurs, immediately disable run and reset timer, whether timing incomplete/complete. New demand full 5s. Count increment once on FALSE-to-TRUE transition of BLOWER_RUN. Init off/count zero.

Need scan semantics: at scan k sample inputs once, q pre-scan retained, outputs after execution, q next updated. Timer elapsed zero first eligible sampled invocation; dt_ms elapsed wall since previous invocation. No unobserved past stability. Need explicit 4-stage scan order: 1 edge sampling, 2 safety/reset priority & state transitions, 3 unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF, 4 unified output assignments.

Need state_machine list of states and transitions. Could model states IDLE, DELAY, RUN? But careful with timer and run. The requirement: permit and delay. If permit true, start timer; after 5s run. If permit false during delay or run, immediately off and reset. If permit true again, full 5s. Count on false->true of run. Could states:
- OFF: BLOWER_RUN false, timer reset, cycle count retained. Transitions to DELAY when permit true.
- DELAY: BLOWER_RUN false, timer timing. Transitions to RUN when permit true and delay elapsed >=5000ms; to OFF if permit false.
- RUN: BLOWER_RUN true. Transition to OFF when permit false. Maybe stay if permit true. But if in RUN and permit true, no timer needed. If loss permit off and reset. This is enough. But timer also in OFF? We can timer reset. Use TON? Need unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF. Timer plan: TON StartDelay (IN := permit and state in DELAY? Actually call unconditionally; PT 5000ms). Reset conditions: permit false, E-stop active, DO_LOW false, state OFF/RUN? Need design.

Need consider scan execution order and timer FB call. Stage 3 "unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF" means timer call at top-level with input expression computed in stage 2? We can define TimerEnable := (state = DELAY) or maybe permit? Need timer timing only while waiting. On entering DELAY from OFF when permit true, timer should start at zero on first eligible sampled invocation; run after >=5s. In PLC TON: input IN true starts; elapsed increments from 0. If state DELAY, call TON with IN := TRUE maybe. Reset when permit false. But if we transition OFF->DELAY in stage 2 based on permit true, then stage 3 call TON with IN := (state = DELAY) AND permit. If state transition to DELAY happened same scan, timer call sees IN true and elapsed? Timer elapsed time zero on first eligible sampled invocation; good. At elapsed>=5000, stage 2? Wait transitions in stage 2 occur before timer call stage 3. If transition to RUN depends on timer.Elapsed >= PT, but timer called later stage 3. Need use previous scan timer elapsed? Need order: stage 2 safety/reset priority & state transitions, then stage 3 unconditional timer calls, then stage 4 outputs. If state transitions need timer Q, use prior timer state from previous scan. But when state is DELAY and timer Q becomes true at stage 3, state transition to RUN would happen next scan. That might delay one scan. Is that acceptable? Requirements say run after conditions remain satisfied for 5 seconds; one scan latency maybe okay? But formal assertions might expect BLOWER_RUN true when delayDone. Need align.

Alternative: stage 2 determines state transitions except RUN promotion maybe uses timer from previous scan. Stage 3 calls timer. Stage 4 outputs computed from state and timer? Could set BLOWER_RUN = (state=RUN) or (state=DELAY and Timer.Q)? But then state transition and output could happen same scan when timer Q true after stage 3. But count edge in stage 2? Hmm stage 4 unified output assignments can compute output directly from permit and timer Q. Need count increment on false->true BLOWER_RUN. Edge sampling stage 1 samples previous outputs or runPrev. But count update in stage 2? It needs know new run. If output determined in stage 4, count cannot be updated in stage 2 based on new run unless compute predicted run in stage 2 or use prior. Could compute NextBlowerRun in stage 2 and count. But requirement explicit 4-stage scan order: 1 edge sampling, 2 safety/reset priority & state transitions, 3 unconditional timer FB calls, 4 unified output assignments. This suggests cycle count edge detection may be in stage 2? It can use previous observed BLOWER_RUN and a logical run command computed in stage 2? Or stage 1 edge sampling samples previous BLOWER_RUN. Stage 2 can update count if next BLOWER_RUN transition? Need stage 2 "state transitions" might compute state and count maybe based on state? But output assignment stage 4. We can define in stage 2: compute State next and CycleCountPulse if (state transition to RUN) or (predicted BLOWER_RUN rising). But if timer Q is from stage 3, run transition may occur in stage 4 not state. Hmm.

Need produce architecture plan not actual code. We can specify scan order and state machine enough. Need formal assertions over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Need use port names DO_LOW, AERATION_E_STOP_NC, BLOWER_RUN, AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT. Could include assertions like G((DO_LOW & AERATION_E_STOP_NC) ...). But formal_assertions optional. Need be careful with LTL syntax and names. We can include normalized from specs maybe use permit/delayDone? They request over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Use only port names in formulas; can use variables? "over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names" likely formulas should refer to these. Could include A1 G(!(DO_LOW & AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> !BLOWER_RUN) maybe safety. Need include delay? Can't refer delayDone unless declared? We can avoid optional? It says optional list. But maybe better include simple assertions only port names. Need not be exhaustive. Must be valid JSON. Need perhaps include formal_assertions with formulas using port names. Need consider temporal / invariant assertions. Could include:
A1: G((!DO_LOW | !AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> !BLOWER_RUN) (if permit false, run off)
A2: G((BLOWER_RUN & X(!BLOWER_RUN)) -> ...)? Not needed.
A3: G((!BLOWER_RUN & X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT = prev?)) Can't use prev. Avoid.
Could include initial: A0: !BLOWER_RUN & AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT=0 at init? LTL G? Formal assertions can be temporal. Use init? But over port names. Maybe: A1 G((!DO_LOW | !AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> !BLOWER_RUN). A2 G(BLOWER_RUN -> (DO_LOW & AERATION_E_STOP_NC)) equivalent but only if delay done not included. A3 G((!BLOWER_RUN & X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT = AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT + 1)) invalid because X same variable both? LTL cannot compare next to current? Could write G((!BLOWER_RUN & X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT = (AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT + 1))) but both under X refer next count? Ambiguous. Better omit cycle count assertions. The prompt says optional list; can include simple. Need not include all.

Need state_machine as list states and transitions. We can represent objects. Need include state names, description, entry actions, transitions. Need maybe distinguish "OFF" vs "WAIT_DELAY" vs "RUN". Transitions:
- OFF -> DELAY if permit true (DO_LOW && AERATION_E_STOP_NC)
- OFF -> OFF if !permit
- DELAY -> RUN if permit && StartDelay.Q (or Elapsed >= 5000ms)
- DELAY -> OFF if !permit
- DELAY -> DELAY if permit && !StartDelay.Q
- RUN -> OFF if !permit
- RUN -> RUN if permit
Maybe safety reset from any -> OFF if !permit. Could define priority transition Any -> OFF when !permit. But state machine list transitions can include. Need maybe in RUN if permit true stays. If emergency stop occurs, !AERATION_E_STOP_NC, permit false -> OFF immediate. If DO_LOW false -> OFF. Good.

Timer plan: TON_StartDelay (TON) PT 5000ms; called unconditionally at stage 3 with IN := (State = DELAY) AND DO_LOW AND AERATION_E_STOP_NC. Reset condition: !permit or State != DELAY or reset command; set state? For TON, IN false resets elapsed to 0. Need reset on loss permit. Also reset when OFF or RUN. Need maybe a second R_TRIG for cycle count? Timer plan can mention edge detection R_TRIG BlowerRunRise, no PT. But "timers required" could include only TON. Need mention R_TRIG not timer. Could include "StartDelayTimer". Maybe "CyclePulse" not timer. Need reset conditions clear.

Priorities: safety first, emergency stop, DO_LOW loss, timer reset, state transitions, cycle edge count, outputs. Need mention E-stop NC semantics.

Initial values: BLOWER_RUN := FALSE; AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT := 0; StartDelayTimer.IN := FALSE; StartDelayTimer.PT := T#5s; StartDelayTimer.ET := 0; StartDelayTimer.Q := FALSE; State := OFF; RunPrev := FALSE; maybe CountPrev := 0; Permit := FALSE; etc. Need initial_conditions includes delayElapsed_ms=0. JSON types: numbers/bools.

Scan execution order: explicit 4-stage array. Need stage 1 edge sampling: sample inputs once; latch RunPrev := BLOWER_RUN? But note BLOWER_RUN is output, previous observed. At first scan before invocation output init false. Need sample rising edge? For count, need detect false->true of BLOWER_RUN. If stage 1 samples RunPrev = prior BLOWER_RUN (pre-scan retained). Stage 2 state transitions and safety/reset; compute NextRun? Stage 3 timer call. Stage 4 output assignments including count? But count needs edge. We can put count update in stage 2? The explicit stage 4 is "unified output assignments" likely assigns outputs, including count. Need define count update in stage 4 using edge sample and new BLOWER_RUN. But stage 2 state transitions maybe not. The stage order says stage 2 safety/reset priority & state transitions, stage 4 unified output assignments. We can place cycle count increment in stage 4 along with BLOWER_RUN assignment: after computing new BLOWER_RUN, if RunPrev = FALSE and new BLOWER_RUN = TRUE then AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT := AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT + 1 else retain. But is that "unified output assignments"? Yes. But stage 1 edge sampling samples previous observed BLOWER_RUN. Stage 2 state transitions sets State and timer reset commands. Stage 3 timer call. Stage 4 computes output BLOWER_RUN from state/timer? Hmm if state transition to RUN depends on timer Q, but timer called stage 3. Need state transitions in stage 2 cannot use new timer Q. Could instead stage 2 handle only resets and state transition to DELAY/OFF; stage 4 compute BLOWER_RUN = (State=RUN) or (State=DELAY and StartDelay.Q). But then State not updated to RUN until next scan. Count increments when BLOWER_RUN true, which can happen in stage 4 based on timer Q while State still DELAY. Next scan stage 2 transitions DELAY -> RUN. That works but state may linger. However output assignment uses timer Q. Count increments in stage 4 using RunPrev and new BLOWER_RUN. Need count increment on same invocation that changes end-of-scan BLOWER_RUN false->true. Good. But if state still DELAY and timer Q true, output true. Next scan stage 2 transitions to RUN; output true; no count. Fine. But if permit false, stage 2 transition to OFF and timer reset? Stage 3 timer call with IN false resets Q at end. Stage 4 output: If using state and timer Q, but timer Q might still be old true in stage 4 because TON call maybe updates Q? Actually stage 3 updates Q based on IN false, so Q false. State OFF, output false. Good. But immediate disable on same scan? Stage 2 priority resets state to OFF; stage 3 resets timer; stage 4 output false. Good.

Alternative: Stage 2 transition DELAY->RUN using StartDelay.Q from previous scan; stage 4 output = state RUN. Then output true one scan after timer Q. Count. But formal maybe okay. To satisfy P1 exactly "G(BLOWER_RUN <-> (permit & delayDone))", if delayDone can be considered timer Q after stage 3, output should be true same scan when timer Q true. Using stage 4 output = (state=RUN) OR (state=DELAY && StartDelay.Q) with state DELAY when permit true. Need ensure if permit false, not true. Good. But if state=RUN and permit true, output true. If state=RUN and permit false, stage 2 transitions to OFF before output. Good. If state=DELAY and timer Q true and permit true, output true; state not RUN until next scan. Then count increments. Next scan state RUN. Works. But is state transition from DELAY to RUN in stage 2 using StartDelay.Q previous scan? At scan after timer Q true, stage 2 sees StartDelay.Q true (from previous scan) and moves to RUN. Output true. Count? RunPrev was true from previous scan, so no increment. Good. This creates one scan where output true while state DELAY. That's fine.

But stage 3 timer call: if state transitioned to RUN in stage 2, IN := (State=DELAY && permit) false, resets timer. That resets Q after output? Wait stage 3 before stage 4. If state moved to RUN in stage 2 (because previous timer Q true), stage 3 calls timer with IN false, resets Q to false. Stage 4 output from state RUN true (permit) so true. Good. But if state still DELAY, timer call IN true, Q true. Output true. Good. So okay.

Need maybe define State transitions:
- Stage 2: if !permit: State := OFF; ResetTimerReq := TRUE; RunCmd? 
- else case State:
  OFF: if permit then State := DELAY; else OFF
  DELAY: if StartDelay.Q (from prior scan) then State := RUN; else DELAY
  RUN: if permit then RUN else OFF
But if StartDelay.Q becomes true in stage 3 and state remains DELAY, stage 4 output true. Next scan stage 2 sees Q true, moves to RUN. Good. Need count in stage 4 on new output. Use RunPrev sampled stage 1. But note if output true in stage 4 while state DELAY and timer Q true, count increments. Next scan stage 2 moves RUN, stage 3 resets timer Q false, stage 4 output true (state RUN), no count. Fine.

But there is an issue: Stage 3 timer IN := (State = DELAY) AND permit. If stage 2 state transitions to RUN, timer resets. If stage 2 state transitions to OFF due permit false, resets. If stage 2 OFF->DELAY, timer IN true, starts at zero. Good.

Could also compute output BLOWER_RUN := permit AND (State=RUN OR (State=DELAY AND StartDelay.Q)). But if stage 2 state still DELAY and timer Q true, output true; if next scan state RUN, timer Q reset false but output from state RUN. Good. If stage 2 state OFF due !permit, output false regardless. Need not include permit in expression if state transitions already handle, but include for safety priority.

Need count update stage 4:
IF NOT RunPrev AND BLOWER_RUN THEN
  IF AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT < 65535 THEN AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT := AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT + 1; END_IF
END_IF
But assumptions tests below overflow. Could just increment. Need avoid count if output true initially? RunPrev init false, output init false first scan until delay. Good.

Need "edge sampling" stage 1: sample inputs into temp? Since scan semantics inputs sampled once at k. We can specify:
1. Edge sampling: read DO_LOW, AERATION_E_STOP_NC once into scan-local image; runPrev := BLOWER_RUN (pre-scan observed); maybe countPrev? Also compute Permit := DO_LOW AND AERATION_E_STOP_NC. But if using port names, okay. Maybe "R_TRIG" not used? Edge sampling can store RunPrev. Cycle count edge detected stage 4. But stage 1 is edge sampling. Need explicit. Maybe also sample reset edge? Only rising edge of BLOWER_RUN. So stage 1: RunPrev := BLOWER_RUN; Permit := DO_LOW & AERATION_E_STOP_NC. Since output BLOWER_RUN pre-scan retained. For first scan, RunPrev := FALSE (init). Need note "no unobserved past stability assumed".

Stage 2: safety/reset priority & state transitions. In stage 2, apply if NOT permit => State := OFF; ResetTimer := TRUE; else state transitions. Also if emergency stop active (AERATION_E_STOP_NC FALSE) or DO_LOW FALSE, same. Since permit false. Need maybe set State OFF before case. Also if state transition to OFF, reset timer. We can define StartDelay.IN in stage 3 from state not stage 2.

Stage 3: unconditional top-level timer FB call outside CASE/IF: StartDelay(IN := (State = DELAY) AND DO_LOW AND AERATION_E_STOP_NC, PT := T#5S); Actually if state OFF/RUN, IN false resets. Need call every scan. Also maybe if safety reset, IN false. Good.

Stage 4: unified output assignments:
- BLOWER_RUN := (DO_LOW AND AERATION_E_STOP_NC) AND ((State = RUN) OR (State = DELAY AND StartDelay.Q));
- IF NOT RunPrev AND BLOWER_RUN THEN AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT := AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT + 1; END_IF;
Need count assigned every scan? It is retained; no else. Could also "AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT := AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT + BOOL_TO_UINT(rising)" to unified. Good.

Need formal assertions. Could include:
A1: G((!DO_LOW || !AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> !BLOWER_RUN) — immediate off when no permit. But P2 says loss of permit clears run and timer; assertion only output. Use "||" valid? JSON string. Could use "G((NOT DO_LOW OR NOT AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> NOT BLOWER_RUN)" but LTL syntax maybe "G((!DO_LOW || !AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> !BLOWER_RUN)". Good.
A2: G(BLOWER_RUN -> (DO_LOW && AERATION_E_STOP_NC)) — run implies permit. Redundant.
A3: G((BLOWER_RUN && X(!BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT >= AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT)) bad.
Could include initial assertion: "init: !BLOWER_RUN && AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT=0" but formal_assertions expects formula G(...)? The prompt says optional list of {"id", "formula": "G(...)"}. It might expect G formula. Could include A0: "G(BLOWER_RUN -> (DO_LOW && AERATION_E_STOP_NC))". A1: "G((!DO_LOW || !AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> !BLOWER_RUN)". A2: "G((!BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT > 0))" weak. But not necessary. Maybe include cycle count non-decreasing: G(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT >= 0) trivial. Better avoid invalid. We can include two safety invariants and one "G((!BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT != 0))" not meaningful. Could include "G((!BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT >= 1))" only first start. Not general. Could include "G((BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT = AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT))" issue as next both. Hmm.

Formal assertions optional; can include just A1 and A2. The user may expect formal assertions list. "optional list" means can omit? They asked "Return complete JSON with keys: ... formal_assertions: optional list". Safer include non-empty list. Need use port names. We can include:
A1: "G((!DO_LOW || !AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> !BLOWER_RUN)"
A2: "G(BLOWER_RUN -> (DO_LOW && AERATION_E_STOP_NC))"
A3: "G((!BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT >= 1))" This is not universally true if count could be 0 at later start? Count non-decreasing, after first start count>=1. At first rising edge yes. But if initial count not zero? Init zero. This assertion says any rising edge implies next count >=1. True for all starts if count increments and never decrements. But if count wraps? excluded. Fine.
A4: "G((BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT >= 1))" not needed.
Could include "G((!BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT > AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT))" invalid semantics. Avoid.

Need maybe include cycle count not increment while run stays true: "G((BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT = AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT))" Under X both same? This means next count equals next count, tautology. Not good. Could use "G((BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT = AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT))" no.

We can include only safety. That's okay.

scan_execution_order: array of 4 strings or objects. Explicit:
1. "Edge sampling: read DO_LOW and AERATION_E_STOP_NC once; latch RunPrev := BLOWER_RUN (pre-scan observed, initialized FALSE); compute Permit := DO_LOW AND AERATION_E_STOP_NC."
2. "Safety/reset priority and state transitions: if Permit is FALSE, force State := OFF and request timer reset; else execute CASE State: OFF->DELAY when Permit TRUE; DELAY->RUN when StartDelay.Q TRUE; RUN->RUN while Permit TRUE; any other condition stays."
Need include "StartDelay.Q is prior-scan value at this stage; same-scan Q is handled by output stage." But maybe not. Could mention in stage 3.
3. "Unconditional top-level timer FB call outside CASE/IF: StartDelay(IN := (State = DELAY) AND DO_LOW AND AERATION_E_STOP_NC, PT := T#5S); call every scan so IN=FALSE resets ET/Q."
4. "Unified output assignments: BLOWER_RUN := (DO_LOW AND AERATION_E_STOP_NC) AND ((State = RUN) OR (State = DELAY AND StartDelay.Q)); IF NOT RunPrev AND BLOWER_RUN THEN AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT := AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT + 1; END_IF; all other outputs held; RunPrev updated only by next scan stage 1." Wait RunPrev update? Stage 1 at next scan. But if stage 1 samples RunPrev at start, after stage 4 BLOWER_RUN changes, RunPrev remains old until next scan. That is correct. But if we say "RunPrev updated only by next scan stage 1" good. Need maybe count update on same invocation. Good.

Potential issue: Stage 4 BLOWER_RUN expression includes StartDelay.Q after stage 3. If State = DELAY and permit true and Q true, run true. But State transition to RUN in next scan. If State = DELAY and Q false, off. If State = RUN and permit true, run true. If State OFF, off. Good.

Potential issue: When State RUN and permit false, stage 2 sets OFF; stage 3 timer IN false; stage 4 BLOWER_RUN false. Good.

Stage 3 resets timer because state RUN (IN false) -> Q false; stage 4 BLOWER_RUN = state RUN true. Good. Count? RunPrev from previous scan when output became true while state DELAY. So no increment. Good. But wait on the scan when Q first becomes true: stage 2 sees prior Q false, stays DELAY. Stage 3 call TON with IN true, Q becomes true (ET >= PT). Stage 4 output true, count increments. Next scan stage 1 RunPrev = true. Stage 2 sees prior Q true, transitions to RUN. Stage 3 resets Q false. Stage 4 output true. Count no increment. Works.

Potential issue: At scan when permit first true from OFF: stage 2 state OFF -> DELAY. Stage 3 TON IN := (State=DELAY) & permit true => starts. Stage 4 BLOWER_RUN = permit AND (State RUN OR (State DELAY AND Q)). TON Q false. Off. Good. Timer elapsed? TON first invocation with IN true; ET maybe 0. It will count dt from next invocation. Requirement "Timer elapsed time is zero on first eligible sampled invocation; dt_ms is elapsed wall time since previous invocation". So after first invocation ET=0. At elapsed>=5s, run true at scan where ET >= 5000. Good.

Need formal assertions maybe include A4: "G((!DO_LOW || !AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> X(!BLOWER_RUN))"? But safety immediate at output stage same scan. P2 says G(!permit -> (!BLOWER_RUN & X(!delayDone))). We can include A1 same-scan. Use "G((!DO_LOW || !AERATION_E_STOP_NC) -> !BLOWER_RUN)". A2 "G(BLOWER_RUN -> (DO_LOW && AERATION_E_STOP_NC))". A3 maybe "G((!BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT >= 1))". But if count overflows? excluded. Fine. Could include "G((BLOWER_RUN && X(BLOWER_RUN)) -> X(AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT >= 0))" trivial. Not include.
